first_impression.summary_in_own_words: A planning service that will organise a wedding in Portugal for Aussie, US and UK couples, with one advisor. The top tells me the legal minimum is one month and that lots of people just do a symbolic thing over there. No price anywhere at the top, so I already know I'm going to have to ask.

attention_map.quote: a legal wedding in Portugal for foreign couples starts at least one month ahead
attention_map.why: An actual number in the first two lines, not fluff. That buys a scroll.

attention_map.quote: with one Wedded Advisor from first enquiry to the wedding weekend
attention_map.why: Every planner says 'one point of contact'. It is not proof of anything.

The button says check my date, the small print says 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms dates and venues with you.' So it doesn't check anything, it's a lead form with a nicer label. That's the kind of thing that makes me wonder what else is dressed up.

attention_map.quote: Planned by Wedded Concierge, with one Wedded Advisor from enquiry to the wedding weekend.
attention_map.why: Called a proof strip but there's no proof in it. No number of weddings, no years, no reviews. It's the same sentence as the hero, again.

attention_map.quote: roof works with scaffolding run to the first quarter of 2027
attention_map.why: Pretty, guidebook stuff. Credit for admitting the scaffolding, nobody else tells you that. But the Algarve card is the vaguest card: 'Clifftop and beach settings on Portugal's southern coast.' That's it?

Five cards, five times 'Ask your Wedded Advisor' for guest numbers, and five times the exact same 'spring and autumn, as a national guide', even for Madeira. It looks templated. If you can't tell me how many people fit, I can't compare this against the tab next to it.

attention_map.quote: state events can cancel bookings at Queluz or the National Palace of Sintra. Nothing may be fixed to the heritage.
attention_map.why: This is the catch, and they told me. Plus a link to the official rules. This is the most trustworthy bit on the page. But then what? If the state cancels my date, what do you do? Nothing said.

attention_map.section: See why couples marry in Portugal
attention_map.quote: Of all the Europe wedding destinations we plan, Portugal gives couples five things in one country.
attention_map.why: 'We plan' but nothing showing they have planned a single Portugal wedding.

attention_map.section: What your Wedded Advisor checks in every venue contract
attention_map.quote: VAT: whether each quote includes VAT, so totals compare like for like.
attention_map.why: Finally, someone talking about hidden costs. Buy-outs, rooms you don't fill, minimums, VAT. This is exactly my worry and it's the only real reason on the page to use them over going direct.

attention_map.section: Plan step by step: Marrying legally
attention_map.quote: The civil registry charges a fee for the ceremony.
attention_map.why: The legal tab is genuinely good, with government links and a 'checked October 2026'. Better than the other tabs I have open. But 'charges a fee' with no number is weird when everything around it is so specific. The US line does the same: 'a consular notarial fee applies.' How much?

attention_map.quote: Every other timing below is advice, not a rule.
attention_map.why: Separating the official rule from their advice is honest. I checked: one month in the hero, the tab, the timeline and FAQ 1 and 5 all match. Six months to marry matches too.

attention_map.quote: What a wedding in Portugal costs depends on five things: your guest count, the region, the season, how many nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use.
attention_map.why: A whole tab called Costs with zero numbers. Not even a ballpark. 'Depends on five things' is what everyone says before they upsell you. This is where I'd close the tab if I was being strict.

attention_map.section: See what a Portugal wedding weekend includes
attention_map.quote: There is no set Portugal package. Instead, your Wedded Advisor helps you plan a weekend around your guests, and it can include:
attention_map.why: The heading says 'includes' and then it's 'can include'. No price, no what's in, no what's out. 'An on-the-day coordinator' is just a bullet on a maybe list, so I still don't know who's actually there if something goes wrong.

attention_map.quote: Exclusive use can mean paying for rooms your guests do not fill
attention_map.why: Same point as the contract box, repeated. Fine, but no new info.

attention_map.quote: Gather family at a wine quinta for a long lunch among the terraces.
Your Wedded Advisor is your one contact at Wedded Concierge, instead of one conversation per venue.
attention_map.why: Okay, that is a reason. But 'Portugal properties are still being confirmed' for Wedded Privileges sounds like they're new to Portugal.
No idea when. Short form, budget optional, fine.

attention_map.quote: There is no single average: the cost depends on your guest count, the region, the season, the nights you take the venue and whether you book it for exclusive use.
attention_map.why: Legal FAQs are solid and consistent with the tabs. The cost FAQ dodges the question it literally asks: 'How much is an average wedding in Portugal?' and no number. Beach permit answer is now on the page about six times.

attention_map.quote: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez's wedding
attention_map.why: Celebrity gossip links where real client weddings should be. Reads like a magazine, not a planner with a track record.

questions_answered.question: What is NOT included in the from price?
questions_answered.evidence: There is no from price at all, and no inclusions or exclusions list. Costs tab and FAQ 4 say only 'depends on five things'. The weekend list is 'can include'. The venue contract box hints at extras (buy-outs, minimums, VAT) but that's the venue's catch, not theirs. I have no idea what Wedded Concierge itself charges.

questions_answered.question: Are these facts consistent across the page?
questions_answered.evidence: One month minimum, six months to marry, five regions, four airports (LIS, OPO, FAO, FNC), beach permit rule and the five Sintra venues all match wherever they appear. Only nit: Monserrate works 'first quarter of 2027' in some places and 'early 2027' in the palace box, which is close enough.

questions_answered.question: What proof is there that this team has done this venue before?
questions_answered.evidence: Proof strip has no numbers. No real Portugal weddings, no reviews, no named venues they've worked with. 'Weddings we plan' is a claim only. The only weddings linked are Ronaldo's and a pop star's.

questions_answered.question: Why book through you and not the venue directly?
questions_answered.evidence: 'one contact at Wedded Concierge, instead of one conversation per venue' and the contract check for 'rooms, buy-outs, minimums and VAT before you sign'. That's a real reason, but without knowing what the service costs me I can't weigh it.

questions_answered.question: What happens if something goes wrong on the day?
questions_answered.evidence: Only 'An on-the-day coordinator' as something a weekend 'can include'. Nothing on what they do if a palace booking is cancelled for a state event, rain plan beyond 'plan a covered option', or supplier no-shows.

objections_triggered.objection: From price with no inclusions list means hidden costs
objections_triggered.triggered_by: No price anywhere; Costs tab and FAQ 4 fallback give no figures; 'The civil registry charges a fee for the ceremony.'; 'a consular notarial fee applies.'

'Planned by Wedded Concierge, with one Wedded Advisor from enquiry to the wedding weekend.' in a strip with nothing to back it; 'Of all the Europe wedding destinations we plan'; no real weddings shown

objections_triggered.objection: Inconsistent numbers (capacity or rooms differ in two places)
objections_triggered.triggered_by: Not triggered on numbers. Guest capacity is never given ('Guests: Ask your Wedded Advisor'), so there is nothing to compare, which is its own problem.

objections_triggered.objection: Labels that promise more than they deliver
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'Check your date' button that does not check a date; heading 'See What a Portugal Wedding Weekend Includes' followed by 'it can include'; 'Proof strip' with no proof

objections_triggered.objection: Nothing on what they do when things go wrong
objections_triggered.triggered_by: 'state events can cancel bookings' with no word on what happens next

trust_signals_noticed: Official government source links for every legal and entry rule, with 'Checked October 2026'
Admitting the catches: state event cancellations, nothing fixed to the heritage, Monserrate scaffolding
The venue contract checklist: rooms, buy-outs, per day or per guest minimums, VAT 'so totals compare like for like'
Clearly labelling 'our advice' versus 'official rule' in the timeline
Numbers consistent across the hero, tabs and FAQ
No superlatives, no urgency, no 'only 3 dates left'
turn_offs_noticed: Zero price information anywhere, including a section literally called Costs
Templated region cards: same 'Best months' line and 'Ask your Wedded Advisor' five times
Celebrity wedding links in place of real client weddings
Beach permit sentence repeated about six times
'Ask your Wedded Advisor' as the answer to almost every specific question

emotional_response.overall: Grudging respect for the honesty on the legal side, frustration on cost. It feels careful not to lie, but careful not to commit either.
emotional_response.trust: Medium on facts, low on the company's own track record.
emotional_response.anxiety: Upsell worry not settled at all: they'll explain 'what drives cost' on a call, which is exactly the call I don't want to get stuck on.

payload.decision_reason: My rule is I only enquire if no cost question is left open, and every cost question is open: no from price, no ranges, not even the registry fee. Nothing proves they've done a Portugal wedding before. I'd keep the tab for the legal-by-passport section, which is better than anything else I've got open, but I'd enquire with whoever puts a number on the page first.
payload.verbatim_reaction: Honestly, this is the most straight-up page I've read today on the legal stuff, and I couldn't catch it out on a single number. But there's a tab called Costs with no costs in it, an FAQ asking 'How much is an average wedding' that won't say, and a 'proof strip' with no proof. Where are your actual Portugal weddings? Why am I looking at Ronaldo's? 'Ask your Wedded Advisor' isn't an answer, it's a sales call. What's the catch on your fee? Bookmarked for the paperwork section, not enquiring.
